Q1.problem_type_and_essence: precedence-constrained DAG scheduling that reduces peak live-buffer residency without violating cache/topology constraints

baseline.name: Kahn ready-set list scheduling + FREE-first + critical-path/slack + incremental-memory tie-break
six_hour_plan: maintain ready set; execute legal FREE early
rank remaining nodes by critical path/slack and incremental live-memory delta
replay Cmax on all six workloads and save one result registry
baseline.why: deterministic, transparent, near-linear/log-linear and gives a strong contest baseline before stochastic search

why_fit: greedy list scheduling scales to large DAGs
type/size/criticality can directly encode memory-pressure and path urgency
determinism is attractive under contest time constraints
author_route.evidence_boundary: paper describes Type+Size+Criticality, but printed appendix calls undefined priority/critical-path/cache helpers, so the claimed composite priority is not implementation-traceable

major_alternatives.why_can_work: same feasible topological-order search and can escape greedy local choices
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only when matched-budget multi-seed evaluation materially beats deterministic baseline

major_alternatives.why_can_work: discrete feasible local refinement is natural after a deterministic schedule
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when structured move-level tabu implementation is repaired and wins on common evaluator

major_alternatives.why_can_work: provides exact/near-exact gap rather than another heuristic label

not_recommended.why_not_now: no large graph-instance training distribution or evidence that policy training pays back within contest budget
spends most evaluations on weak or infeasible schedules and gives poor reproducibility

switch_conditions: retain MCBGS only if explicit components are implemented and ablation shows stable value
add stochastic refiner only if it beats baseline under same evaluator/time budget
use exact solver calibration whenever graph size permits

Q2.problem_type_and_essence: buffer-lifetime/cache-address allocation with spill/reload decisions to minimize extra DDR movement under capacity and overlap constraints

input_target_constraints.input: fixed schedule + buffer size/type/lifetime/use pattern + cache capacities
input_target_constraints.objective: minimize true incremental transfer bytes, with runtime secondary/lexicographic unless explicitly normalized

baseline.name: lifetime sweep + deterministic Best-Fit free-list + min incremental-transfer spill victim + farthest-next-use tie-break
six_hour_plan: allocate with Best-Fit or linear-scan free list
on overflow compute exact additional spill bytes for each legal victim
choose minimum-cost victim and replay all constraints/bytes
baseline.why: simple, debuggable and directly tied to the real byte objective

author_route.method: MOACADSA-style First-Fit allocation + dynamic spill/caching reuse heuristic
why_fit: spill score can use lifetime and COPY_IN semantics
cache reuse can reduce repeated movement
author_route.evidence_boundary: abstract says Best-Fit, body/code use First-Fit; paper victim equation uses argmin while code reverse-sorts a different size*lifetime score and picks the largest

major_alternatives.why_can_work: buffer lifetimes are intervals and memory reuse resembles register allocation
major_alternatives.when_prefer: large deterministic workloads where speed/reproducibility matter

major_alternatives.why_can_work: reports lower transfer than S027 on Conv_Case0 and provides another audited heuristic route
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only after shared evaluator aligns spill semantics

major_alternatives.why_can_work: can benchmark allocator/spill quality and validate constraints
major_alternatives.when_prefer: small buffer sets or decomposed time windows

not_recommended.why_not_now: poor transfer efficiency and unstable evidence
units/scales make weights non-interpretable; hard byte objective should not be hidden

switch_conditions: do not call allocator Best-Fit unless code actually chooses smallest fitting hole
do not promote spill heuristic until paper/code choose same score direction and variables
use sophisticated search only if deterministic allocator materially misses shared-evaluator optimum/benchmark

Q3.problem_type_and_essence: minimize total execution cycles while bounding additional transfer generated by a resource-aware reschedule

input_target_constraints.input: Q2 feasible mapping/baseline + schedule/resource timing model
input_target_constraints.independent_evaluation_unit: one workload graph; cross-workload joint optimization requires explicit shared-resource coupling

baseline.name: epsilon-constraint lexicographic local search: enforce transfer cap first, then minimize cycles
six_hour_plan: freeze Q2 baseline from same Result Registry
set official transfer cap epsilon and reject any violating candidate
apply resource-aware topological swap/insert or list rescheduling
choose lowest-cycle feasible result and report per-case cap slack
baseline.why: matches the hard-constraint nature of the task and avoids arbitrary unit-weight scalarization

author_route.method: DOSA incremental dual-objective scheduling / multi-sequence collaborative optimization narrative
author_route.evidence_boundary: printed appendix calls undefined _apply_optimization_strategies; most evaluation code processes each task case independently, and 10%/15% transfer tolerance drifts across sections

major_alternatives.model: Large Neighborhood Search under epsilon cap
major_alternatives.why_can_work: can destroy/repair local schedule blocks while enforcing hard transfer limit
major_alternatives.when_prefer: medium-large DAG where exact solve is too slow

major_alternatives.model: NSGA-II / MOEA only after shared evaluator
major_alternatives.why_can_work: can map the actual cycle-transfer frontier
major_alternatives.when_prefer: when stakeholders need multiple operating points and all hard constraints are replayed

major_alternatives.why_can_work: gives optimality gap and cap verification

not_recommended.why_not_now: can trade away a hard transfer limit and weights depend on unit scaling

not_recommended.model: paper-labeled multi-sequence joint optimizer without shared-state code
not_recommended.why_not_now: naming coordination without executable coupling overstates evidence

switch_conditions: source one official epsilon from problem contract; do not mix 10% and 15%
only call result multi-sequence collaborative if code/evaluator jointly couples multiple sequences/resources
only use Pareto/MOEA when actual feasible nondominated points and selection rule are shown
